subject: Large SE's - interpreting and next steps

messages.subject: Large SE's - interpreting and next steps
parts:
Hi all,

I'm a modeling newbie and I've been working with Unmarked for that past few weeks trying to produce occupancy models for my environmental DNA data. I took 3 water samples from ~50 vernal pools and I'm looking at a few different species (modeled separately). I simultaneously dip-netted each pool and am treating that data as a Known Occupied Site with KnownOcc right now and modeling with the basic occu() model.

I only really care about detection rate, rather than occupancy rate. I have some covariates that might be important to detection (pool area, water volume filtered, type of filter, GPS/property I was sampling). 

For each species, I produced 16 models with a combination of the different covariates. But it looks like SEs for each covariate for each model is pretty big. Even for the model I ran with no covariates (~ 1 ~ 1 ) I had a pretty large SE:

Call:
occu(formula = ~1 ~ 1, data = b)

Occupancy:
 Estimate   SE    z  P(>|z|)
     -1.4 0.25 -5.6 2.12e-08

Detection:
 Estimate   SE    z P(>|z|)
     4.08 1.01 4.04 5.3e-05

AIC: 114.696 

For the more complicated models things get even worse, even though the AIC is "better":

Call:
occu(formula = ~site + area + vol ~ 1, data = b, knownOcc = which(brme$Dipnet == 
    1))

Occupancy:
 Estimate  SE       z P(>|z|)
    -13.9 157 -0.0887   0.929

Detection:
             Estimate      SE         z P(>|z|)
(Intercept)   -7.8126    3.70 -2.11e+00  0.0349
siteDutchman  15.5936  344.33  4.53e-02  0.9639
siteJepson    15.9373   55.67  2.86e-01  0.7747
siteUCM        2.5489    2.41  1.06e+00  0.2903
siteWerre     -0.0989 1783.71 -5.54e-05  1.0000
area         -25.5845   12.73 -2.01e+00  0.0444
vol            2.2266    1.68  1.33e+00  0.1838

AIC: 59.29502 

I'm having trouble interpreting what these huge numbers mean, other than that these models aren't working right. Unsurprisingly, when I use Predict() to look at detection rates, my SEs there are also huge.

Does this mean that none of my covariates seem to correlate with detection rates at all and I should throw them out? Should I try a different type of model? Really I'm only interested in the detection rate and how it changes based on how many water samples I take. I'm not quite sure what my first steps should be for finding the problem, or how to determine what's "too big" in terms of SE (the model with no covariates still has an SE that is bigger than my gut is comfortable with but I don't know how to establish that with numbers).

Thank you!

messages.author: 5fb191f8527859e2
messages.subject: Aw: [unmarked] Large SE's - interpreting and next steps
parts:
Dear Shannon,
The estimate of detection in your occu(~1 ~1) model is 4.08 (an SE of 1.01 is ok, I think). If you back transform the estimate to the probability scale
exp(4.08)/(1+exp(4.08))
you get 0.9833736. This means that detection is almost perfect (a rare event!). If detection is close to 1, then it is not surprising that covariates don't matter and that the estimates and their SE are large.
Hope this helps.
Best,
Beni
